home_claddagh_fisher.text: The Claddagh was a fishing village with its own elected 'king', who settled quarrels on the quay.
The old thatched cottages were cleared in the 1930s. I live in what is left, with an extra-long view of the water.
Pierlords guard the harbour wall like landlords. Keep your sandwich in your bag and you will be fine.

then.text: There you are, pet. Will you use the kitchen? Go on, sure it's no bother.

else.text: Come in, come in, you're letting the heat out. Sit. Have you eaten? You haven't. I can tell.
I'll give you the barmbrack, the way my mother made it. There's a ring in it, so chew careful.
And a Brigid's cross and a shamrock pin. They'll mind your creatures when I can't.
Pop in whenever you've got the makings. You can use my kitchen.
